Definition: from G4111; moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false):--feigned.
BiblicalUsage: Plastos means moulded, made up — feigned, artificial. Peter uses it once, in 2 Peter 2:3: false teachers shall with feigned words make merchandise of you.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe made-up words are the false teacher's stock in trade, and the buyer always pays.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
